Modified assessment using the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS): The May 3, 2023 FOMC statement is guarded-hawkish—citing moderate growth, robust job gains, elevated inflation, a 25 bp hike to 5–5.25%, and ongoing balance-sheet runoff—while acknowledging that tighter credit conditions will weigh on activity. The April 2023 SLOOS materially reinforces and deepens that caution. Banks reported broad-based tightening in C&I lending (to firms of all sizes), commercial real estate, and multiple consumer categories (credit cards, autos, residential real estate, HELOCs), with wider spreads, higher loan rates, lower LTVs, and stricter DSCRs. Demand weakened notably for C&I credit (capex, M&A, inventory, and A/R financing) and CRE, and banks expect to tighten further. Reasons cited include a weaker economic outlook, reduced risk tolerance, deteriorating collateral values, higher funding costs, deposit outflows, and liquidity concerns; foreign banks reported similar patterns. These SLOOS findings imply a clearer, near-term credit contraction than the statement alone conveys, increasing downside risks to growth and employment and likely easing inflation pressures over time. Net effect: shift from near-neutral to moderately negative.
